article_title: COVID-19-related differences in students’ verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany
citation: Rebecca Schneider, Sebastian Weirich, Poldi Kuhl, Stefan Schipolowski, Petra Stanat. (2025). COVID-19-related differences in students' verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany. Learning and Instruction 100 (2025) 102228. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102228
title: IQB Trends in Student Achievement large-scale assessment data (IQB-BT 2021 and IQB-BT 2022)
description: Representative German large-scale educational assessment datasets providing achievement scores in reading, listening, and orthography for cohorts before and after the pandemic restrictions. The article states: "Our analyses are based on data from German large-scale educational assessment studies with achievement scores available for student cohorts prior to the COVID-19 pandemic (T1) and for student cohorts affected by the pandemic-related restrictions (T2)." Sampling used a stratified multi-stage random selection process; items were administered via a multiple matrix sampling design with a Common-Item Nonequivalent Groups Design linking to compare subgroups with different mean ability. Data include student, parent, teacher, and principal questionnaires.
requirements: Case weights to make data representative for students at regular and special needs schools
Multiple imputation and replication procedures for clustered samples in analysis
constraints: The authors state they do not have permission to share the data
target_learners: Grade 4 and Grade 9 students in Germany, including students with SEN-L at regular and special needs schools
target_learning_goals: Verbal competencies in reading, listening, and orthography based on German national educational standards
examples: The IQB-BT 2021 study supplied the Grade 4 2016/2021 cohorts and the IQB-BT 2022 study the Grade 9 2015/2022 cohorts analyzed here
key_sources: Rebecca Schneider, Sebastian Weirich, Poldi Kuhl, Stefan Schipolowski, Petra Stanat. (2025). COVID-19-related differences in students' verbal achievements: Comparisons of different cohorts of students with SEN based on large-scale assessment data from Germany. article_title: Novice providers' success in performing lumbar puncture: a randomized controlled phantom study between a conventional spinal needle and a novel bioimpedance needle.
citation: Lilja Helmiina, Talvisara Maria, Eskola Vesa, Heikkilä Paula, Sievänen Harri, Palmu Sauli. (2024). Novice providers' success in performing lumbar puncture: a randomized controlled phantom study between a conventional spinal needle and a novel bioimpedance needle. BMC Medical Education 24:520. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05505-z
title: IQ-Tip bioimpedance spinal needle system with real-time CSF detection
description: The IQ-Tip system (Injeq Plc, Tampere, Finland) is a 90 mm spinal needle that senses tissue bioimpedance at the needle tip. It "provides real-time feedback from the needle tip when penetrating the lumbar tissues and informs the physician when the needle tip reaches CSF with an audio-visual alarm." In the study it was used by novice students on a lumbar phantom, requiring no additional devices such as ultrasound imaging.
requirements: Requires no additional devices beyond the needle system itself; the article states its basic use is virtually similar to a conventional spinal needle with no need for additional devices (e.g., ultrasound imaging).
constraints: In two cases the system did not detect saline although the needle tip was in the correct place, confirmed by saline flow after stylet removal.
One author (H.S.) is an employee of Injeq Plc, the system's manufacturer.
target_learners: early-stage (first- to third-year) medical students with no prior lumbar puncture experience
target_learning_goals: performing lumbar puncture successfully and confidently
examples: In the randomized controlled phantom trial, 30 students performed lumbar puncture with the IQ-Tip system after watching a 25-second animation on how the bioimpedance system operates.
